atlas-gb.0220: Applications are online and tests and video interviews remote, but the final stage is often in person in the UK: KPMG’s Launch Pad is a half-day at venues in London, Birmingham, Manchester, Bristol, Glasgow and Leeds. Non-UK citizens need a visa route, and employers want the right to work shown before the start.
atlas-gb.0221: English; extra European languages are an asset in London. The Skilled Worker visa asks for English at CEFR B2.
atlas-gb.0222: Most schemes run in four to six steps: an online form, online tests, a live or recorded video interview, then an assessment centre or final interview. KPMG’s graduate route has four stages: an application with a job-preview quiz, online skills and cognitive tests (the cognitive test is timed at 36 minutes), a video interview of 6 pre-recorded questions put by an AI avatar (about 40 minutes), and a half-day in-person Launch Pad.
atlas-gb.0223: PwC lists seven stages for most programmes: online application, numerical, verbal and logical reasoning tests, a behavioural assessment, a video interview and an assessment centre. It applies a once-a-year rule: one application per cycle, and a failed or withdrawn one means waiting for the next.
atlas-gb.0224: Assessment centres are essentially group interviews: an ice-breaker, a group exercise (often a business case), a group or individual presentation and an individual interview, with time to meet staff. They run from an afternoon to overnight, you are assessed throughout, including informal time, and some are held virtually.
atlas-gb.0225: The Civil Service Fast Stream has five stages: choose up to 4 schemes, online tests (work scenarios, a case study and a data test to finish within 5 days of activation), a timed recorded video interview, an online assessment centre (a written advice exercise, a stakeholder communication exercise and a development conversation) and, on most schemes, a final selection board.
atlas-gb.0226: Dress smartly even for video interviews and choose a quiet room. KPMG requires assessments to be done without outside help or AI tools and can withdraw an application or re-test you if it finds a breach.
atlas-gb.0227: From first test to offer, KPMG gives an offer within 2 working days of the Launch Pad, which runs on set dates from November to May. No source gives a median time for the whole process; it depends on when you apply, because schemes fill in order of arrival.
atlas-gb.0228: Probation has no set statutory length: Acas says it can be any length, and during it you still give the notice in your contract or the statutory minimum.
atlas-gb.0229: The statutory minimum notice is one week from either side once you have been employed for a month, rising for the employer to one week per year of service from two years, up to 12 weeks. A contract can set longer notice, not shorter.
atlas-gb.0230: Offers from large firms come quickly after the final stage and are conditional: KPMG gives an offer within 2 working days of the Launch Pad, subject to immigration status and right to work being confirmed before the start. There is no thirteenth-month salary in the UK; pay is one annual figure.
atlas-gb.0231: Scheme salaries are published and fixed, so there is little to negotiate: ISE’s 2025 average is £33,000 for graduates and £24,000 for apprentices, and the Fast Stream starts at £31,186. KPMG’s sponsored hires must accept their offer at least three months before joining.
atlas-gb.0232: Only employers with a sponsor licence can offer a Skilled Worker visa; the Home Office publishes the register of licensed sponsors. Ask early whether the employer holds a licence and whether the specific programme is covered, because large firms ration it.
atlas-gb.0233: KPMG sponsors only Audit, Tax and Consulting and Technology programmes based in London and all Consulting Actuarial ones; it cannot sponsor any other graduate programme and says this may change at short notice.
atlas-gb.0234: A Graduate visa needs no sponsor, which is why many employers hire on it first: it lasts 2 years for applications made by 31 December 2026 and 18 months after, and cannot be extended, so a sponsor must be found within that time.
atlas-gb.0235: Student visa holders must show the course completion date before the programme start, and a government scholarship that covered fees and living costs needs unconditional written consent to stay in or re-enter the UK.
atlas-gb.0236: The Civil Service Fast Stream takes nationals of the UK, Ireland, the Commonwealth and several European countries who can live and work in the UK, and some security posts need British citizenship; the CyberFirst bursary is for British citizens only. Student Circus lists employers that can sponsor international students.
atlas-gb.0237: Civil Service Careers (civil-service-careers.gov.uk) carries the Fast Stream and government jobs, and its nationality page sets who can apply. Large employers’ own early-careers pages (KPMG, PwC, Deloitte and others) take applications directly.
atlas-gb.0238: TARGETjobs lists graduate jobs and schemes, internships and placements, the UK 300 most popular employers and offers CV review and an interview coach; Prospects, run by Jisc, covers graduate jobs, work experience and employer profiles.
atlas-gb.0239: General boards named by university careers services include Indeed, CV-Library, S1 Jobs and LinkedIn. Student Circus, provided to Imperial students, lists verified full-time and internship jobs from employers that can sponsor international students.
atlas-gb.0240: Employers tour universities in the autumn and large graduate recruitment fairs run in the same term; KPMG holds its Launch Pad assessment days on seven dates in six cities, from London to Glasgow, between November and May. University careers services run the fairs and host employer talks.
atlas-gb.0241: Starting in the wrong window: autumn is the peak and some employers open from July, while graduate programmes usually open in August or September with deadlines as early as October; some multinationals recruit more than a year ahead. A one-year master’s student who begins looking in September is already late.
atlas-gb.0242: Sending the wrong CV: more than two A4 pages, a photo or a date of birth. If the employer asks for one page, send one page.
atlas-gb.0243: Using your single application too early: PwC lets you apply once per cycle, and a failed P&G test means a twelve-month wait, so do the practice tests first.
atlas-gb.0244: Using AI to answer assessments: KPMG can withdraw you, and in the 2025 ISE survey 61% of employers reported candidates using AI in interviews without disclosure.
atlas-gb.0245: Skipping the summer internship or placement that is the real entry route, and assuming sponsorship will be available: it covers only some programmes and can change at short notice.
atlas-gb.0246: Interviews, tests and the assessment centre are in English and fluent business English is assumed; a second European language is an advantage in London. No certificate is asked on the scheme form, though the Skilled Worker visa asks for CEFR B2.
atlas-gb.0247: Case interviews and written exercises are in English, so the evidence is the interview itself rather than a certificate.
atlas-gb.0248: Consumer-goods schemes assess in English through online tests, a video interview and an assessment centre.
atlas-gb.0249: The Fast Stream assesses a written advice exercise and a stakeholder communication exercise at its online assessment centre, all in English.
atlas-gb.0250: Software roles interview in English with coding and technical tests; Revolut’s programme asks for working SQL, Python or R, and no second language is asked.
atlas-gb.0251: Research roles are assessed on publications, coding and maths in English; the Skilled Worker visa baseline is CEFR B2, which a UK degree or an approved test proves.
atlas-gb.0252: Competition is at a record: employers averaged about 140 applications per graduate vacancy in 2025, up 14% on the year and more than three times the 38 of two decades earlier; retail, FMCG and tourism averaged about 290 and legal about 69.
atlas-gb.0253: Among 2022/23 postgraduate-taught leavers, 13% of international graduates were unemployed and seeking work against 3% of UK graduates (Jisc, 2026); graduate unemployment overall rose to 6.1%.
atlas-gb.0255: A licensed university issues the CAS; then apply online. EU citizens verify identity in the UK Immigration: ID Check app and need not upload bank statements, though they must hold the money.
atlas-gb.0256: Up to 20 hours a week in term and full time in official vacations; no self-employment, freelancing or gig work.
atlas-gb.0257: Since January 2024 taught master’s students cannot bring a partner or children; research degrees still can.
atlas-gb.0259: £1,529 a month in London, £1,171 elsewhere, for up to 9 months
atlas-gb.0262: Internships are not allowed as a visitor. Outside a degree, you need a GAE visa through an approved umbrella sponsor such as the British Council or BUNAC: up to 12 months, a supernumerary role paid at least the minimum wage.
atlas-gb.0263: On a Student visa, an assessed placement can take up to half the course.
atlas-gb.0266: After a UK degree, apply from inside the UK before the Student visa ends: any work, no sponsor, once only. Two years if you apply by 31 December 2026, 18 months from 1 January 2027; three years after a PhD.
